A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same few-shot semantic segmentation benchmark. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained results across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments comparing five backbones and five adaptation methods on Cityscapes, COCO, and PPD, including numerical results and learning-rate searches.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and reports additional shot-count, model-factor, learning-rate transfer, and SAM diagnostic results.

M1.justification: The benchmark sampler and five principal adaptation methods remain unchanged. Section 5.5 adds experimental SAM decoder adaptations using a constant prompt, N-class outputs, removal of the IoU branch, and alternative upsampling components. These are localized procedural additions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same segmentation tasks on Cityscapes, COCO, and PPD. Additional shot counts, model variants, resolution changes, and learning-rate transfers operate within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparator set is retained, while Tables 5–8 add comparisons involving DINO V1, convolutional DINO and CLIP variants, and DINO V2 with registers. Section 5.5 also evaluates alternative SAM decoders. The convolutional CLIP comparator is labelled ResNet-101 in Table 6 but ResNet-50 in the prose; its precise identity is inconsistent.

E3.justification: v2 adds 2-, 5-, and 10-shot evaluations, input-resolution sweeps from 224 to 1024, model-size and pretraining comparisons, and explicit source-to-target learning-rate transfer tests. These substantially expand the evaluation design. The stated training procedure and splits for the retained 1-shot experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's qualitative learning-rate transfer discussion becomes a quantified analysis including PPD. v2 additionally investigates shot-count sensitivity, resolution, model size, architecture, pretraining data and objectives, registers, and SAM decoder and mask-distribution hypotheses (Sections 5.2–5.5 and Appendix 8.3).

E5.justification: Both versions specify three fixed random seeds and report mean mIoU with standard deviations. The retained uncertainties are unchanged, and the additional benchmark results follow the same reporting practice. No new statistical tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: The aggregate and per-dataset 1-shot results are unchanged, with v1 Table 2 becoming v2 Table 9. Substantial new results include 71.07 average mIoU for 10-shot DINO V2 full fine-tuning (Table 2) and COCO LoRA scores of 34.02 with registers versus 28.99 without (Table 8). These represent additional experimental conditions.

T1.justification: The support/query formulation, k-shot definition, sampling construction, and mIoU formula are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised in the other.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution, DINO V2's strong performance, and the competitiveness of simple adapters remain central. v2 adds an explicit contribution concerning individual model-design factors and a stronger claim to being the first systematic study of these foundation models' adaptation capabilities.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning resolution fairness, model size, pretraining, architecture, and registers. It qualifies learning-rate transfer for PPD, attributes improved full fine-tuning with more shots to reduced overfitting, and explores SAM failure mechanisms. It also acknowledges differing losses as a confound in the DINO V1/V2 training-dataset comparison.

D1.justification: v2 adds a planned code-release address, clarifies PPD background sampling and validation-based learning-rate selection, and describes the new experimental adaptations. However, it removes v1 Appendix 8.2/Table 3's exact selected learning rates. Common hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information, and training instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Vision Transformers Need Registers, Segmenter, SegFormer, and Convolution Meets LoRA. The existing related-work coverage remains largely intact, while the introduction makes its first-systematic-study positioning more explicit.

P1.justification: The abstract is condensed and rewritten, the DINO explanation expands, Datasets becomes a standalone section, and learning-rate discussion moves into the main experiments section. Much of the existing method, training, related-work, and conclusion prose is retained; the scientific additions account for much of the expansion.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation, with revised headers, figure styling, and table emphasis. v2 adds resolution and shot-count plots, numerous comparison tables, and a model-summary table. The original learning-rate table disappears, while the retained detailed 1-shot table is reformatted and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Sections 5.2–5.5 substantially strengthen the evidence behind the practical recommendations by testing shot-count dependence, the previously acknowledged resolution confound, model factors, and learning-rate transfer. These checks address important sensitivities left untested in v1. Removing exact selected learning rates weakens reproducibility, and some factor comparisons remain confounded or inconsistently labelled, but these limitations are narrower than the gains in empirical validation.
